sentences.text:
This petition is filed u/s.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for claiming compensation on account of death of Kushal S/o Arjun.M.
2.

It is the case of the petitioners that on 16-07-2024 at about 7-15 p.m., within the jurisdiction of Doddaballapura Town Police Station, near Kempegowda Hospital, , Railway Station circle - Raghunathapura road, Doddaballapura Town, when the deceased was 3 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.6674/2024 riding the unoffending Dio Scooter bearing registration No.KA-50-EB-7283 at that time the driver/accused of the offending Lorry bearing registration No.KA-07-B- 3129 from Railway station circle towards Raghunathapura and drove the said offending vehicle in a high speed,
rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life and drove towards extreme left side of the road and dashed against the unoffending vehicle, as a result the rider/deceased of the unoffending vehicle fell down on the right side of the road and left side rear wheel of the offending lorry run over the head of the deceased, as a result the rider/ deceased sustained grievous head crush injuries and died on the spot.
Thereafter, the informant/M. Manjunath lodged complaint before the Doddaballapura Town police station.

Accordingly, a case was registered in their Crime No.108/2024 and prepared F.I.R. for the offence punishable under section 281 and 106 of BNS R/w Section 199(A) of MV Act and submitted to the jurisdictional judicial magistrate and the superior officers and investigation was taken up by the investigating Officer.

3. It is contended that the Petitioner No.1 is the mother and Petitioners No.2 is the father of the deceased Sri.Kushal.A and as on the date of the alleged accident 4 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.6674/2024 the said deceased was aged about 17 years at the time of accident and he was a student perusing 2nd PUC at Sri Narayana PU College, Doddaballapura.
The petitioners have claimed compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- under different head of loss of dependency, funeral and obsequies expenses, loss of filial love, loss of consortium, loss of estate.

Geetha M vs Najeeb Ahmed on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65173532/
2 4

It is contended that the accident is solely due to the rash or negligent driving of the driver of the offending Lorry bearing registration No.KA-07-B-3129 and the respondent No.1 is the RC owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
5. In response to the notice, the respondents No.1 and 2 are appeared through their counsels and filed their respective written statements.

6. In the written statement of respondent No.1, he has admitted that he is the RC owner of the offending Lorry vehicle and denied the petition averments in part including age, avocation, income and negligence attributed against the driver of the offending Lorry vehicle and contended that the driver of the said offending lorry possessing valid and effective driving 5 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.6674/2024 licence and the offending lorry was duly insured with Respondent No.2/Insurance company at the time of alleged accident and any liability, i.e., fastened on him/RC owner would have to be indemnify by the Respondent No.2 and sought for dismissal of the claim petition.

7. In the written statement of Respondent No.2 Insurance Company, it has admitting that the offending vehicle was duly insured with it and the same is valid on the date of the accident and denying the petition averments in part and contended that the Petitioners have not furnished the particulars of the vehicle including the driving licence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Further it is denied having insured the vehicle involved in the accident.
The insurer liability is subjected to validity of the DL, permit and other documents as per the law.
Further it is alleged that there is no compliance of provision under Section 134(C), 158 of M.V. Act.
Further it is alleged that the alleged accident is occurred due to negligence and fault of the deceased and there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The driver of the offending vehicle is not possessing valid DL, FC and effective permit at the time of alleged accident.

As such the insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation and in order to 6 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.6674/2024 obtained compensation the Petitioners have constrained to filed the present claim petition.

Further it is denied that the age, income and occupation of the deceased and the petition is false and frivolous in the eye of law and the quantum of compensation claimed by the claimants is exorbitant and reserves the right u/s.170 of M.V.Act.
Hence sought for dismissal of the petition.

8. On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal framed the following:-
:: I S S U E S ::
1. Whether the Petitioners prove that, they are legal heirs of deceased Kushal.A?
2. Whether the Petitioners prove that on Kushal.
A sustained grievous injuries due to rash and negligent act of driver of Ashok Leyland Lorry bearing registration No.KA-07-B-3129 and dated 16.07.2024 at about 7-15 p.m., and he died on the spot?

Geetha M vs Najeeb Ahmed on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65173532/
3
3. Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?
from whom?
4. What order or award?
9. In support of the case of the Petitioners, the Petitioner No.1 is examined as PW-1 and got marked Ex.P1 to P16 7 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.6674/2024 and closed their side.
The Legal Representative of Insurance Company got examined as RW-1 and got marked Ex.R.1 document and closed their side.
10. Heard the arguments of both side.

11. My findings to the above referred Issues are as under;
 Issue No.1 :- In the affirmative  Issue No.2 :- In the affirmative  Issue No.3 :- Partly in the affirmative  Issue No.4 :- As per final order  for the following.......

:REASONS:
12. Issue No.2 : This petition is filed u/s.166 of M.V. Act  1989 for seeking compensation for the death of the  deceased Kushal.A S/o Arjun.M.
13.

The petitioners' in the petition have contended that on 16-07-2024 at about 7-15 p.m., within the jurisdiction of Doddaballapura Town Police Station, near Kempegowda Hospital, , Railway Station circle - Raghunathapura road, Doddaballapura Town, when the deceased was riding the unoffending Dio Scooter bearing registration No.KA-50-EB-7283 at that time the driver/accused of the offending Lorry bearing registration No.KA-07-B-3129 from Railway station 8 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.6674/2024 circle towards Raghunathapura and drove the said offending vehicle in a high speed, rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life and drove towards extreme left side of the road and dashed against the unoffending vehicle, as a result the rider/deceased of the unoffending vehicle fell down on the right side of the road and left side rear wheel of the offending lorry run over the head of the deceased, as a result the rider/ deceased sustained grievous head crush injuries and died on the spot.
It is contended that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

The Respondent No.1 has admitted that he is the RC owner of the offending vehicle vehicle and his version is that, the driver of the offending vehicle is possessing valid and effective driving licence, permit and the offending vehicle was duly insured with Respondent No.2/Insurance company and any liability, i.e., fastened on him would have to be indemnify by the Respondent No.2 and sought for dismissal of the claim petition.

The Respondent No.2/Insurance Company admitted the alleged accident and the offending vehicle was duly insured with it and its version is that, the alleged accident occurred due to the negligence and fault of the deceased and no fault of the driver of the offending vehicle, however, slowly he 9 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.6674/2024 may be driving and therefore he cannot be held to be negligent.

Further it is alleged that the driver of the Geetha M vs Najeeb Ahmed on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65173532/
4 offending vehicle is not possessing valid DL and effective permit at the time of alleged accident.
Hence there is violation of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
As such the insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation and in order to obtained compensation the Petitioner has constrained to filed the present claim petition.

Further it is denied that the age,
income and occupation of the deceased and the petition is false and frivolous in the eye of law and the quantum of compensation claimed by the claimant is exorbitant and sought for dismissal of the petition.
14.
The burden to prove the framed issues lies on the Petitioners.

Hence, in order to prove their case,
the Petitioner No.1 herself examined as P.W.1 and he has reiterated the entire petition averments and contentions taken in the course of claim petition in his evidence before this Court and also produced as many as Exs.P.1 to P.16 documents.
Therefore, there is no necessity to repeat those facts again.
I have gone through the documents produced by the PW-1.

Ex.P-1 is the True copy of FIR, Ex.P-2 is the copy of Complaint, Ex.P.3 is the Spot Mahazar, Ex.P.4 is the Spot Sketch, Ex.P.5 is 10 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.6674/2024 the Vehicle seizer mahazar, Ex.P.6 is the Motor Vehicle Accident report, Ex.P.7 is the Inquest report, Ex.P.8 is the Postmortem report, Ex.P.9 is the Charge Sheet,
Ex.P.10 is the SSLC marks card, Ex.P.11 is the 1 st PUC marks card, Ex.P.12 is the Adhar Card of deceased, Ex.P.13 is the College I.D. Card of the deceased, Ex.P.14 and Ex.P.15 are the Adhar Cards of Petitioners, Ex.P.16 is the Ration Card.
15. In the cross-examination of PW-1 by the Respondent No.2 he has deposed that the complainant Manjunath is her brother and he informed her regarding the alleged accident.
Further she has denied that the said Manjunath has lodged false complaint against the driver of the offending vehicle.
Further she has deposed that she is the RC owner of the unoffending vehicle.
At the time of accident her deceased son was aged about 17 years 10 months and he was not possessing valid and effective LL and DL to ride the vehicle.
Further she has denied that the offending vehicle is falsely implicated and the said vehicle is no nexus to the alleged accident.
Further she has denied that at the time of accident her deceased son was not wearing helmet and he do not know to ride the unoffending vehicle and due to his fault the alleged accident occurred.
At the time of accident 11 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.6674/2024 the driver of the offending vehicle run the wheel of the said vehicle on the head of the deceased.
Further she has denied that she has not incurred Rs.1,00,000/- towards funeral and transportation.
Further she has deposed that at the time of accident the deceased was perusing 2nd PUC and therefore he is non-earnings.

Further she has denied that in order to get more compensation in collusion with the police they have falsely implicated the offending vehicle and filed false case against the offending vehicle and produced concocted created documents and filed false evidence affidavit and deposing falsely.

During the cross examination Pw.1 has consistently deposed on the lines of the petition/prosecution case and she has made those versions,
which could not be shattered in cross examination.
16.

In order to prove the version of respondent No.2, the respondent No.2 got examined its Legal Representative as R.W.1 and he has reiterated the entire version averments and contentions taken in the course of written statement in his evidence before this Court and also he has produced as many as Ex.R.1 document.
Therefore, there is no necessity to repeat those facts again.
I have gone through the documents produced by the RW-1.
Ex.R.1 is the Copy of the Insurance Policy.

sentences.text: The alleged accident occurred due to negligence and fault of the rider of the unoffending vehicle and no fault of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The police have filed false Charge Sheet.
The Charge Sheet is filed against the Petitioner No.1, as she has permitted her deceased minor son to ride the unoffending vehicle.
Further she has denied that the alleged accident occurred due to negligence and fault of the driver of the offending vehicle and no fault of the rider of the unoffending vehicle.
Further she has denied that in order to escape from the liability she has filed false evidence affidavit and deposing falsely.

17. On careful reading of Ex.P6/MVA report it specifies that the Motor Vehicle Inspector has been clearly opined that, the said incident did not occur because of the mechanical defects in respect of the said offending and unoffending vehicles.
Further the said Inspector noticed the damages to the offending vehicle and opined that, front left side corner bumper scratched.
Further the said Inspector noticed the damages to the unoffending vehicle and opined that, head light cover scrutinized, front right side body dent and damaged.
On going through the Ex.P-8/Postmortem report it is seen that Doctor opined that cause of death of deceased is due to head injury sustained in the alleged road traffic accident.

19. On going through the Ex.P3/spot Mahazar it is seen that in pursuance of the alleged Ex.P2/complaint on 17.07.2024, the police have visited the spot and the complainant/Manjunath has shown the spot to the police and the police have conducted the detailed spot mahazar, in the presence of panch witnesses and during the mahazar the police have prepared Ex.P.4/Spot Sketch therein.

20. On going through the Ex.P-2/Complaint it is seen that on 16-07-2024 at about 7-15 p.m., near Kempegowda Hospital, , Railway Station circle - Raghunathapura road, Doddaballapura Town,
when the deceased was riding the unoffending Dio Scooter bearing registration No.KA-50-EB-7283 at that time the driver/accused of the offending Lorry bearing registration No.KA-07-B- 3129 from Railway statio279 and 304A of IPC. n circle towards Raghunathapura and drove the said offending vehicle in a high speed, rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life and drove towards extreme left side of the road and dashed against the unoffending 14 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.6674/2024 vehicle, as a result the rider/deceased of the unoffending vehicle fell down on the right side of the road and left side rear wheel of the offending lorry run over the head of the deceased, as a result the rider/ deceased sustained grievous head crush injuries and died on the spot.
The alleged accident occurred due to the negligence and fault of the driver of the offending vehicle.

21. The Respondent No.2 contended that the accused is innocent and falsely implicated by the police and counsel further contended that the alleged accident occurred due to no fault of the accused and however, slowly he may be driving and therefore he cannot be held to be negligent.

Admittedly, the accused is the driver of the offending vehicle and further admitted that, deceased was dead due to grievous injuries sustained by him in the alleged accident caused by the offending vehicle in Geetha M vs Najeeb Ahmed on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65173532/
6 question.

On going through the prosecution papers, FIR, Complaint, Spot Mahazar, Spot sketch,
MVA Report, Inquest mahazar, Postmortem report and Charge Sheet and the evidence of PW-1 is specific to the effect that, the driver of the offending vehicle/accused is the reason for the said incident and at his instance, the incident took place.
The alleged accident was occurred 15 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.6674/2024 due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.

The evidence of Pw.1 was corroborated to the case of the prosecution and they have supported the manner of occurrence in their evidence in the court and the manner of occurrence is the same as alleged in the Ex.P2/complaint.

It seems that Pw.1 has clearly made those versions,
which could not be shattered in cross examination.

Therefore, considering the above discussed aspects collectively, it is the considered opinion of the Court that, the incident having been taken place in the manner asserted by the prosecution and the same being proved to have been taken place in the manner alleged by the prosecution, the accused drew the offending vehicle in a rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life and at the spot dashed to the deceased Kushal.A as a result he sustained grievous injuries and died due to alleged accident.

In view of the police records,
it clearly establishes that the alleged accident occurred at the spot.
It is not in dispute as to the aspect that, the deceased Kushal.A died on the spot in the alleged accident.
Because, for the above reasons collectively, it is clear that, the accident happened due to rash or negligent act of the accused.
It is evident that injuries and cause of death of deceased Kushal.A S/o Arjun.
M 16 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.6674/2024 noted in the Ex.P8/PM report would be caused by a road accident.
At the same time, it has come out in evidence that the alleged accident was occurred due to rash or negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.
Matters being so, the acts of the accused person clearly constitute the offences punishable under sections 281 and 106 of BNS R/w Section 199(A) of MV Act.
Thus because of such negligent act of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle, it resulted in the death of the innocent child Kushal.A S/o Arjun.
M aforesaid, as the driver of offending vehicle/accused drove the said offending vehicle very rashly or negligently on the spot.
Therefore, the alleged accident occurred due to the fault of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle.
Accordingly I answered Issue No.2 in the Affirmative.
22. Issue No.1 and 3:-
The Learned Counsel for the Petitioners contended that the deceased was aged about 17 years at the time of accident and he was pursuing 2nd PUC.
The Petitioner No.1 is mother and Petitioner No.2 is the father of the deceased.

Further the Counsel contended that as per the Judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram reported in 2018 17 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.6674/2024 ACJ 2782, the Petitioners being legal heirs and dependents of deceased, each of the Petitioners are entitled for compensation under the head of loss of love and affection consortium and prays to award the compensation as prayed in the petition.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 23. On the other hand the learned Counsel for Respondent No.2 contended that the Petitioners are not entitled for compensation towards future prospects and hence prays dismissal of the petition.
24. On going through the Ex.P-12, Ex.P-14 and Ex.P.15/Adhar Cards of the Petitioners and deceased, it is seen that the Petitioner No.1 is the father and Petitioner No.2 is the mother of the deceased.
Hence on the strength of Ex.P-12, Ex.P-14 and Ex.P.15/Adhar Cards it is crystal clear that the Petitioners are the legal representatives and dependents of the deceased.

Geetha M vs Najeeb Ahmed on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65173532/
7 25.

The petitioners have contended that as on the date of the accident the deceased was aged about 17 years and the petitioners relied on the Ex.P-12/Adhar Card of the deceased, wherein the date of birth of the deceased is shown as 15.09.2006.
The accident was occurred on 16.07.2024.
Hence it is clear that as on the date of the accident the deceased was aged about 17 years 10 months.
Hence the age of the deceased is considered as 17 years.
It is not in dispute that the deceased died in the road traffic accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver.

The alleged accident is occurred in the year 2024, in this regard in the authority reported in order dated 12.09.2024, NC:
2024:KHC:38401 in MFA No.11440/2011 C/w MFA No.206/2018 in the case of Lakshminarayanappa @ Moogappa and Others V/s M.S. Royal Sundaram Allianz Insurance Company Ltd., and another of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka,
Bengaluru., wherein it is held that the sum payable for the death of a minor killed in a motor vehicle accident by adopting the average of the two methods for every year from 1984 till date would be the ideal methodology for determine the compensation payable to the parents of a minor who is killed in a road accident.

entities.text: Lakshminarayanappa @ Moogappa and Others V/s M.S. Royal Sundaram Allianz Insurance Company Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly a ready reckoner of the sums payable to a single parents as well as both parents who lost a minor children aged above 15 years and below 18 years of age in a motor vehicle accident for an accident occurring in each year from 1994 till date is as given in table 3.4.

In view of the position of law and a ready reckoner given in table 3.4 in the above decision, this is a case in which an accident occurred in the year 2024, in which deceased Kushal.A, a 17 year old was killed 19 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.6674/2024 and his mother and father (both parents) are claiming compensation.

As per the method of determination of compensation made in the above decision, as per table 3.4, both his parents would be entitled for a compensation of Rs.20,19,768/-.
27.

Thus I conclude that the Petitioners are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.20,19,768/-.
28.
Hence, the respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the award amount.
However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fixed on the respondent No.2/Insurance Company and it is directed to deposit the compensation amount.
Thus I conclude that, the Insurance company/Respondent No.2 is directed to the deposit the compensation amount along with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of filing of the claim petition.
Hence, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative and issue No.3 partly in the affirmative.

29. Issue No.4: for the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the Petitioners under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby Partly allowed with cost.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The alleged accident was occurred 15 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.6674/2024 due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.
The evidence of Pw.1 was corroborated to the case of the prosecution and they have supported the manner of occurrence in their evidence in the court and the manner of occurrence is the same as alleged in the Ex.P2/complaint.
Therefore, considering the above discussed aspects collectively, it is the considered opinion of the Court that, the incident having been taken place in the manner asserted by the prosecution and the same being proved to have been taken place in the manner alleged by the prosecution, the accused drew the offending vehicle in a rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life and at the spot dashed to the deceased Kushal.A as a result he sustained grievous injuries and died due to alleged accident.
In view of the police records,
it clearly establishes that the alleged accident occurred at the spot.
It is evident that injuries and cause of death of deceased Kushal.A S/o Arjun.
At the same time, it has come out in evidence that the alleged accident was occurred due to rash or negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.
Matters being so, the acts of the accused person clearly constitute the offences punishable under sections 281 and 106 of BNS R/w Section 199(A) of MV Act.
Thus because of such negligent act of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle, it resulted in the death of the innocent child Kushal.A S/o Arjun.
Therefore, the alleged accident occurred due to the fault of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle.
24. On going through the Ex.P-12, Ex.P-14 and Ex.P.15/Adhar Cards of the Petitioners and deceased, it is seen that the Petitioner No.1 is the father and Petitioner No.2 is the mother of the deceased.
Hence on the strength of Ex.P-12, Ex.P-14 and Ex.P.15/Adhar Cards it is crystal clear that the Petitioners are the legal representatives and dependents of the deceased.
The petitioners have contended that as on the date of the accident the deceased was aged about 17 years and the petitioners relied on the Ex.P-12/Adhar Card of the deceased, wherein the date of birth of the deceased is shown as 15.09.2006.
The accident was occurred on 16.07.2024.
Hence it is clear that as on the date of the accident the deceased was aged about 17 years 10 months.
Hence the age of the deceased is considered as 17 years.
It is not in dispute that the deceased died in the road traffic accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver.
opennyai_summary.arguments: Further the Counsel contended that as per the Judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram reported in 2018 17 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.6674/2024 ACJ 2782, the Petitioners being legal heirs and dependents of deceased, each of the Petitioners are entitled for compensation under the head of loss of love and affection consortium and prays to award the compensation as prayed in the petition.
